title: Observability candidate scratch - Sofia Martinez
content:
Candidate: Sofia Martinez (sophia.martinez@gmail.com) - phone screen + onsite notes. Role: Senior Observability Engineer (inference telemetry). Interviewers: Morgan Ellis (owner), Aisha Khan (sre/alerts), Dev Patel (serving-runtime).

High-level impression:
- Strong domain familiarity: solid past work building sampling layers and low-overhead tracing for high-throughput ML infra.
- Communicates clearly, pragmatic tradeoff approach.
- Some weaknesses in low-level implementation details (Rust/unsafe memory) but has good systems intuition and strong product sense.

Detailed notes by segment:
1) Background (5-7 min)
- 7 years infra/observability at two startups; last role focused on telemetry for recommenders and feature-store.
- Implemented a custom collector that pre-aggregated metrics across 10k+ model instances to reduce ingestion costs.
- Familiar with Prometheus, OpenTelemetry (collector + instrumentation), Grafana/Tempo, and Lightstep-type sampling.
- Mentioned experience with per-customer cost attribution and per-route token accounting for model inference.

2) System design: "Design tracing and metrics for inference platform" (35 min)
- Goal framed well: capture latency/quality/cost signals without overwhelming cardinality.
- Proposed multi-tier sampling: deterministic front-line sampling by customer tier + reservoir sampling for error traces, plus dynamic rate adjustment based on trace budget.
- Suggested using hashed keys for high-cardinality fields (request id, user id) to keep some signal while bounding storage.
- Recommended pre-aggregation at edge: emit summary counters per-minute and ship only representative spans for heavy requests.
- Thoughtful about SLOs: differentiate P99 for tail latency vs median; advocated for distinct alerting policies for production-critical customers.
- Good on rollout strategy: feature flags for sampling policy, A/B testing sampling thresholds, and metrics to validate not losing critical signals.

Weakness / follow-up question: wanted more concrete latency budget math around impact of sampling on deriving accurate P99. Ask for a 15–30m follow-up to walk through math with a small dataset.

3) Coding prompt: "Write a sampler that prioritizes error traces and maintains a bounded sample size per minute" (40 min)
- Pseudocode approach: combination of priority queue + reservoir sampling. Wrote clean pseudocode; edge cases mostly covered (clock skew, minute boundaries).
- Not fully implemented data structures but described concurrent-safe approach with sharded queues.
- Missed a lock-free optimization detail I asked about; admitted would prototype using sharded atomics.
- Overall coding/problem-solving: pragmatic and clear, slightly slow on micro-optimizations.

4) Deep dive: instrumentation for inference cache hits / KV cache telemetry (15 min)
- Knew where to place hooks: on request dispatch, after KV-cache lookup, and on final token emission.
- Suggested emitting lightweight markers (cache_hit boolean, cache_latency_ms) and a compact sampling of spans for cache misses.
- Good suggestion: correlate cache miss rate with downstream model latency and per-token cost to build a feature for cache tuning.

5) Culture / collaboration (10 min)
- Emphasizes pragmatic docs, runbooks, and automation to reduce toil.
- Comfortable pairing with product and runtime teams to scope instrumentation.

Scoring (subjective, scale 1-5):
- Domain knowledge (observability patterns, telemetry stacks): 5
- System design (scalability/rollout): 4
- Coding/problem solving: 4
- Ownership/communication: 5
- Culture fit: 4
- Overall: 4.25 -> strong senior, maybe staff after 6–12mo.

Recommendation + rationale:
- Recommend: Hire with small take-home follow-up OR Strong onsite -> offer.
- Rationale: deep product-aligned experience (model-cost telemetry), solid design thinking, would unblock observability work for inference quickly.
- Caveat: would like to validate concurrent/low-latency implementation details via a short follow-up task.

Proposed follow-ups (action items):
- 1) Short take-home (2–4 hours) to implement a sampler (reservoir + priority) in our language of choice (Go preferred). Deliverables: code + 1-page note on invariants, concurrency model, and complexity. (Assigned: Morgan to send prompt)
- 2) Practical check: ask for a snippet or explanation of a real incident where their sampling strategy missed a signal and how they adapted. (Ask Aisha to probe during reference checks)
- 3) Reference checks: two engineering managers from previous role; ask specifically about running experiments and cross-team rollouts. (Assigned: Dev)

Questions / TODOs to myself:
- Confirm compensation band expectations (ask recruiting) and whether they are open to staff ladder after 6 months.
- Add candidate to the "observability-candidates" tracker and link JIRA-ENG-1423.
- Draft offer language around interview-to-prod ramp and initial priorities: sampling layer + dashboards for model cost.
- Create small repo template for take-home to reduce friction (boilerplate + tests).

Raw Clip quotes: (paraphrased)
- "We need to accept that we will never sample everything — the job is to make sure we sample the right things and be able to backfill when necessary."
- "I prefer deterministic sampling tied to customer tiers because that makes post-hoc billing and debugging easier."

Notes to self: keep technical bar for concurrent structures high for this role — if they pass the take-home and can justify their lock-free choices, move forward quickly. If not, consider extending offer at Senior with clear expectations and a 6-month technical check-in.

Slack refs / links to include in final debrief: #eng-observability thread from 2026-03-01 about sampling budgets, PR 678 (placeholder) that touches the collector config, and confluence instrumentation guidelines.

End of scratchpad.

-- Morgan
